final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative surface substitution with maximal PLM plausibility (1.0) and the highest homolog mutant frequency among candidates (0.325). Low-risk change unlikely to impair receptor binding or entry while modestly improving thermostability.

Valine-to-isoleucine is a classic hydrophobic core packing substitution for enhanced thermostability, supported by PLM 1.0 and MSA frequency 0.267 with good applicability. Conservative change preserves overall fold and function.

PLM plausibility is very high (1.0) and the leucine-to-isoleucine change is a conservative hydrophobic substitution. MSA frequency is low (0.067), so confidence is reduced but stability benefit remains plausible.

stop_reason.detail: Phenotype predictor unavailable and all applicable evidence tools have been exhausted on the candidate pool; further rounds would not change the final Top-3.

history.rationale: Introduces a charged residue in a solvent-exposed head loop away from the receptor-binding site, mirroring common avian H5 variants; may increase environmental/thermal tolerance via improved surface electrostatics.
Same uninformative WT-mismatch status; no change in substantive evidence, minor confidence trim.

Highest combined support: ESM-1v fully neutral-plausible (1.0) and 33% homolog frequency, the strongest evolutionary tolerance in the pool. Surface glycan-site-adjacent change; conservative N→D keeps polarity while reducing deamidation liability.
PLM plausibility 1.0 and the best MSA mutant frequency (0.325) among active candidates; conservative surface substitution unlikely to impair entry.
Conservative substitution at an internal head-core position frequently tolerated in influenza A HA lineages; valine is highly represented in natural variants, suggesting a mild stability benefit.
Uninformative WT-mismatch; conservative substitution still plausible, minimal trim.
Valine is smaller than isoleucine, so this typically reduces core packing and stability; zero MSA frequency further disfavors it.
Stem-region (HA2 proximal) hydrophobic core substitution that can improve packing and thermostability of the HA trimer without affecting fusion peptide or receptor-binding functions.
Position 345 has no coordinates in 2FK0, so structural stability impact cannot be verified for a core stability objective; trimmed confidence.
PLM-neutral and 27% homolog frequency with good coverage; hydrophobic core-like substitution away from receptor-binding site, plausibly improving packing thermostability.
Isoleucine/valine swaps are classic thermostabilizing core hydrophobic packing changes; PLM 1.0 and MSA 0.267 support evolutionary tolerance.
Beta-strand position in the head distal from RBS; isoleucine substitution increases hydrophobic packing and has been reported in thermostable HA variants.
Structure evidence returned a WT-mapping mismatch rather than a residue-level score, so it is uninformative rather than negative; confidence reduced only marginally pending PLM/MSA evidence.
PLM score 0.36 is mildly unfavorable despite decent homolog tolerance (0.05); downgraded but retained given its proximity to receptor-binding region stability rationale.
Lowest PLM score among candidates (0.361) and low MSA frequency; T318 is near receptor-binding region head positions where changes can impair entry.

rejection.reason: Lowest PLM score among candidates (0.361) and low MSA frequency; T318 is near receptor-binding region head positions where changes can impair entry.

history.rationale: Surface-exposed position adjacent to but not within the receptor-binding pocket; aspartate is common among homologs and may enhance stability of the 190-helix region.
Evidence uninformative (mapping mismatch); retained at prior confidence pending sequence-level evidence.
N193 sits in a glycosylation-adjacent region of HA head; introducing a charge with zero evolutionary support risks entry-function loss.

rejection.reason: N193 sits in a glycosylation-adjacent region of HA head; introducing a charge with zero evolutionary support risks entry-function loss.

history.rationale: HA2 stem core substitution that improves helix packing in the trimer interface; stem-stabilizing mutations are well documented to raise HA heat tolerance while preserving fusion competence.
No coordinates in 2FK0 and no toxin data; less support for a stability claim, trimmed.
PLM-neutral with modest homolog tolerance (0.075); conservative β-branched substitution in HA2 stem region compatible with folding stability goals.
Very high PLM plausibility, but MSA frequency is low (0.067); still a reasonable conservative hydrophobic core substitution for stability.
Transmembrane-proximal hydrophobic core position; a conservative isoleucine substitution can stabilize the trimer stem bundle and is unlikely to disrupt cell entry.
TM-region position with no structural coverage; stability gain unverifiable structurally, trimmed.
Transmembrane-region isoleucine could stiffen the TM anchor, but MSA applicability is only 0.39 and frequency 0.051, weakening support.
Conservative charge-preserving substitution on an exposed loop of the HA1 vestigial esterase domain; may slightly improve local stability without affecting antigenic or functional sites.
Uninformative; conservative substitution retained at low confidence.
Low PLM (0.37) and near-zero homolog frequency; only weakly retained as a charge-shortening conservative option.
Low PLM plausibility and negligible MSA support; minimal stability benefit expected.

rejection.reason: Low PLM plausibility and negligible MSA support; minimal stability benefit expected.

history.rationale: Position 189 is on the receptor-binding-proximal region but arginine is naturally common at this site in H5 homologs; conservative and may stabilize the local structural element.
Uninformative structure result; conservative charge-preserving mutation retained.
PLM-near-neutral (0.96) but essentially absent in homologs (0.005); conservative charge-preserving change, retained with low confidence.
High PLM plausibility but near-zero MSA frequency; arginine is longer and can alter a nearby salt bridge, so kept mid-tier.
Proline at a loop position (130-loop) can rigidify the backbone and improve heat stability; risk of local conformational change warrants moderate confidence.
Proline introduction near a receptor-proximal region carries entry-function risk and no supporting evidence emerged; downgraded to reject candidate.
Proline substitution has the worst PLM score (0.045) and zero MSA support; S145 lies in a head-loop region important for antigenic/entry function.

rejection.reason: Proline substitution has the worst PLM score (0.045) and zero MSA support; S145 lies in a head-loop region important for antigenic/entry function.
